source_evidence: Fixed indexed annuities earn interest during the accumulation phase based, in part, on the performance of a specified benchmark
answer: A fixed indexed annuity is a deferred annuity whose interest is linked in part to a benchmark index over a specified term. The insurer credits interest at the end of the term, so you do not know the rate in advance. The interest credited cannot be less than zero, even if the market falls, but limits can restrict how much you earn when the index rises. In other words, the annuity’s credited interest is connected to index performance, but it is not simply the index’s full return.
